data.narrative:
Zeta Surgical is a Seed-stage biotech company that has raised $9M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 public companies in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses total capital raised ($9M) as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Seed to the subsequent financing stage, yielding an implied valuation of $22M. The Public-Comp Anchoring approach cannot be deployed because the target's revenue is not on file—standard practice for private-stage companies. The Peer-Median method is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data points within the biotech sector; while 7 same-sector peers exist, none meet the narrow stage or valuation-tier filters required for reliable triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $19M to $26M, centered on $22M. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of single-method valuation at Seed stage. Key risks include the absence of revenue data to validate public-company multiples and the scarcity of precisely comparable private Seed-stage biotech benchmarks. Additional diligence on product development stage and capital efficiency would refine this estimate.
